top_temples.name: Basukinath Temple (Baba Basukinath Dham)
top_temples.location_note: Basukinath's central shrine in Dumka district; the most famous Shiva temple in Bihar and Jharkhand, twin pilgrimage circuit with Deoghar.

top_temples.name: Parvati Temple, Basukinath
top_temples.location_note: Directly facing the main Shiva shrine within the Basukinath temple complex; tradition holds that Shiva and Parvati meet each evening when both temple gates open.

top_temples.name: Jagannath Temple, Bokaro
top_temples.location_note: Near Jawaharlal Nehru Biological Park, Bokaro Steel City; a marble-built replica of the Puri Jagannath Temple.

top_temples.name: Sri Sri Kalika Maharani Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bokaro Steel City; features a 10-ft black stone statue of Kali.

top_temples.name: Ayyappa Temple, Bokaro
top_temples.deity: Ayyappa, with Shiva, Vishnu, Kartikeya, and Ganesha
top_temples.location_note: Bokaro; founded 1983, built in Bengali architectural style.

top_temples.name: Ram Mandir, Bokaro
top_temples.location_note: In the heart of Bokaro city, one of its oldest temples, surrounded by a market and smaller shrines.

top_temples.name: Surya Mandir, Bokaro
top_temples.location_note: Bokaro Steel City.

top_temples.name: Baidyanath Dham (Baba Baidyanath Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Deoghar's defining shrine; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and also a Shakti Peetha, among Jharkhand's most significant pilgrimage sites.

top_temples.name: Naulakha Mandir
top_temples.location_note: About 1.5 km from the Baidyanath Temple in Deoghar; 146 ft tall, its construction reportedly cost nine lakh rupees, architecture resembling Belur Math.

top_temples.name: Taponath Mahadeva Temple, Tapovan
top_temples.location_note: Tapovan Caves, about 10 km from Deoghar; associated with the legend of sage Valmiki's penance.

top_temples.name: Nandi Temple, Nandan Pahar
top_temples.location_note: On a small hill at the edge of Deoghar.

top_temples.name: Kundeshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 20 km from Deoghar; known for its peaceful surroundings.

top_temples.name: Shakti Mandir, Dhanbad
top_temples.location_note: Heart of Dhanbad city; houses an akhand jyoti brought from the Jwalaji Temple in Himachal Pradesh.

top_temples.name: Kalyaneshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Adjacent to the Maithon Dam in Dhanbad district; established in the 19th century, over 500 years of devotional history, known as the 'Lady of Fulfilment'.

top_temples.name: Jagannath Temple, Dhanbad
top_temples.location_note: A prominent temple within Dhanbad city.

top_temples.name: Hari Mandir, Dhanbad
top_temples.location_note: Dhanbad city; a place of worship and meditation.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Dhanbad
top_temples.location_note: Dhanbad city.

top_temples.name: Harihar Dham, Bagodar
top_temples.location_note: Giridih district; home to one of the tallest Shiva lingas in the world at 65 ft, spread over 25 acres, major Shravan Poornima festival.

top_temples.name: Jharkhandi Dham
top_temples.location_note: Near Dhanwar, Giridih district; unusual for its roofless temple structures.

top_temples.name: Samosharan Temple, Madhuban
top_temples.location_note: Madhuban village, Giridih district; a Jain temple over 2,000 years old, part of the base complex for Parasnath pilgrims.

top_temples.name: Bhomiyaji Sthan, Madhuban
top_temples.location_note: Madhuban, Giridih district; a well-known Jain shrine distinct from Samosharan Temple.

top_temples.name: Khandoli Shiv Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Near Khandoli Dam in Giridih district; a locally popular shrine.

top_temples.name: Vishnupuri Temple
top_temples.location_note: Hazaribag city; one of its prominent temples.

top_temples.name: Narsinghsthan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Narsinghsthan village, Hazaribag district; noted for architectural beauty.

top_temples.name: Budhwa Mahadev Mandir, Hazaribag
top_temples.location_note: In the heart of Hazaribag city; believed to be over 100 years old.

top_temples.name: Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Hazaribag city.

top_temples.name: Panch Mandir, Surajkund
top_temples.location_note: Surajkund, Hazaribag district; a well-known temple cluster distinct from the Harihar Dham shrine that lies in neighboring Giridih district.

top_temples.name: Bhuvaneshwari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Bhuvaneshwari Hill (about 500 ft), Jamshedpur.

top_temples.name: Rankini Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jamshedpur; one of the city's well-known Devi shrines.

top_temples.name: Surya Mandir, Jamshedpur
top_temples.location_note: Jamshedpur city.

top_temples.name: Tinplate Kali Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Tinplate area, Jamshedpur; known for its peaceful atmosphere.

top_temples.name: Golpahari Mandir (Gol Pahari Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: On a hilltop outside the main city of Jamshedpur, also called Pahari Mandir.

top_temples.name: Maa Chanchala Devi Temple (Shaktipeeth)
top_temples.location_note: Atop Chanchal Hill in Markacho, Koderma district; a major Navratri pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Bhadrakali Temple, Koderma
top_temples.location_note: About 5 km from Koderma Junction; one of the district's most important religious sites.

top_temples.name: Prachin Shiv Mandir, Khakparta
top_temples.location_note: On a hill in Khakparta village, about 12 km from Lohardaga; an ASI-protected ancient shrine.

top_temples.name: Budhwa Mahadev Temple, Lohardaga
top_temples.location_note: Lohardaga district; believed to be over 500 years old, known for intricate carvings.

top_temples.name: Shikharji Temple (Teerthraj Shikharji)
top_temples.location_note: Atop Parasnath Hill, Giridih district; the holiest Jain pilgrimage site in the world, built in the 18th century, highest peak in Jharkhand.

top_temples.name: Bhomiyaji Temple (Taleti)
top_temples.location_note: At the base of Parasnath Hill, marking the start of the pilgrimage ascent to Shikharji.

top_temples.name: Chhinnamasta Temple (Chinnamastika Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: At the confluence of the Bhairavi and Damodar rivers, Rajrappa; one of the most revered Shakti Peethas in eastern India.

top_temples.name: Kaleshwar Mahadev Temple, Rajrappa
top_temples.location_note: On the same temple campus as Chhinnamasta Temple in Rajrappa, to its east; one of four Mahadev shrines surrounding the main complex.

top_temples.name: Jagannath Temple, Ranchi
top_temples.location_note: Atop a hill about 10 km from Ranchi; built in 1691 by Barkagarh king Thakur Aninath Shahdeo, famous for its Rath Yatra.

top_temples.name: Pahari Mandir, Ranchi
top_temples.location_note: On a 2,140-ft hill in Ranchi; major Maha Shivaratri celebrations.

top_temples.name: Shree Maa Kali Mandir, Ranchi
top_temples.location_note: One of Ranchi's oldest and most famous temples.

top_temples.name: Sun Temple, Ranchi
top_temples.location_note: About 40 km from Ranchi; a modern temple shaped like a chariot with 18 wheels and seven horses.

top_temples.name: Shree Shyam Mandir, Ranchi
top_temples.location_note: A well-known temple within Ranchi city.
